title: State-level optimization: PTET elections, state non-conformity, domicile awareness
summary: Three state-level levers that materially affect after-tax outcomes for pass-through owners, frequently ignored at the federal-planning level.
detailsHtml:
Pass-Through Entity Tax (PTET) election — the operative SALT-cap workaround

OBBBA made the $10K SALT cap permanent (with limited phase-in increases for households under $500K AGI), leaving the PTET election as the standing high-income workaround. As of 2026, 36+ states permit pass-through entities (S-corps and partnerships) to pay state income tax at the entity level — deductible federally under IRS Notice 2020-75 — with owners then receiving a state-level credit for the tax paid. For a CA business owner in the 37% federal bracket with $400K of pass-through income, PTET recovers approximately $13K of otherwise-capped federal SALT deduction annually. State election deadlines vary; many require election by March 15 of the prior tax year (i.e., to elect for tax year 2026, the election was typically due March 15, 2025). Check state PTET-statute specifics (e.g., CA AB 150, NY Tax Law §860 et seq., NJ BAIT). Missed elections are not curable retroactively; the value is meaningful enough that PTET election deadlines belong on a recurring annual planning calendar.

State non-conformity to federal preferences — material in CA, NY, NJ, MA

State conformity to federal Code provisions is not uniform. The high-value non-conformity items: California does not conform to §1202 (the full federal §1202 gain remains taxable to CA at up to 13.3% / 14.4% with SDI cap removed); California, NY, and others have partial non-conformity to §1031 like-kind exchanges and to bonus depreciation. California also imposes the Mental Health Services Tax (1% additional on taxable income over $1M). For a CA-resident founder selling QSBS with $20M of excludable federal gain, the CA tax at 13.3% on the unexcluded portion is meaningful — and the absence of CA preferential capital-gain rates means even fully-federal-excluded gain creates significant CA exposure. NJ does not conform to several federal preferences either. Verify state-specific conformity before assuming federal preferences flow through.

Domicile arbitrage before liquidity events — the highest-magnitude state-level move

For households with substantial unrealized gains, a planned business sale, or a multi-year Roth conversion ladder, establishing residence in a no-income-tax state (TX, FL, NV, WA, TN, SD, WY, AK, NH limited to interest/dividends) 12+ months pre-event can save 7-figure state tax on a $5M+ exit. Domicile-change indicia matter — voter registration, driver's license, primary residence, where you spend the majority of your nights, professional and social ties, dependents in state schools, vehicle registration, professional licenses. Aggressive domicile claims without underlying ties are litigation magnets; CA and NY in particular pursue residency audits aggressively. The full Phase 7 advanced-strategies catalog covers the domicile-change playbook in depth; for now, surface the timing question: if a substantial liquidity event is on the 3-year horizon, the domicile decision needs to happen now, not later.

Reference: IRS Notice 2020-75 (PTET federal deductibility); state PTET statutes (CA AB 150, NY Tax Law §860, NJ BAIT, IL PTE Tax); CA Rev. & Tax. Code §17041 (CA Mental Health Services Tax). Coordinate with state-tax counsel before any aggressive domicile claim; the residency-audit defense burden is on the taxpayer.
